_comment: Reviewed, pragmatic exceptions to the architecture rule that skotiq_core is the only Dart package allowed to import package:skotiq_bridge (docs/architecture.md §1). Only two kinds of file qualify: (1) the desktop headless appliance layer, which IS the local hardware owner on the appliance (the FfiBackend-equivalent at the network seam, architecture §4-5) and legitimately drives Rust directly rather than going back through a network backend; (2) thin UI files that only need a bridge *data type* (an enum/struct) for display, where re-modeling the type in core would be churn for no behavioral benefit. UI files that call bridge *functions* (image processing, stretch, PHD2 control) are NOT whitelisted - those are real boundary leaks and must move behind a skotiq_core role. The audit loader reads only the 'file' and 'reason' keys. See docs/production-readiness/bridge-boundary-plan.md.

allow.reason: Native library bootstrap (bridge.NativeBridge) at process start; pre-backend init, legitimately app-local.
Headless appliance layer: the desktop binary is the local hardware owner (FfiBackend-equivalent at the network seam, architecture §4-5). Cover/calibrator/switch API + state enums.

Headless appliance layer: catches bridge_error.SkotiqError to shape HTTP error responses for the DepthLock goal endpoints on the local hardware owner. The import is used for that typed catch alone — no bridge function is called, the goal work itself goes through the skotiq_core DepthLock backend role. Same reviewed exception already granted to device_handlers.dart, guiding_handlers.dart, run_watch_handlers.dart and validation.dart; the typed match is what keeps these handlers off string-sniffing the error text, which the fail-closed handlers_e_tostring rule forbids.
